claims.text: The initial Mg-containing alloy is produced by high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering.
The ball-milled, SPS-consolidated alloy initially has a homogeneous, metastable, non-equilibrium solid-solution microstructure.
Localized Joule heating occurs near micropores or particle boundaries during SPS.
Localized Joule heating accelerates diffusion and causes phase separation of the metastable alloy.
Low-level oxygen ingress during SPS helps drive decomposition of the metastable solid solution.
Decomposition produces nanoscale Ti- and Zn-rich intermetallic precipitates.
Limited oxygen ingress promotes Ti and possibly Zn segregation into fine, uniformly distributed intermetallic precipitates.
Ti- and Zn-rich intermetallic precipitates act as nucleation sites and oxidize preferentially to produce a coherent TiO2-rich film.
A Ti-rich surface film is associated with passivation and high corrosion resistance in ball-milled, SPS-consolidated Mg-Ti-Zn alloys.
Greater oxygen contamination promotes Mg oxidation and MgO formation.
Excess oxygen causes intermetallic precipitates to coarsen.
Excessive MgO and coarse intermetallics compromise passivation, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Controlled oxygen exposure during SPS preserves corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the initial state.
Uncontrolled oxygen exposure produces more MgO and larger intermetallic phases and consequently diminishes corrosion and oxidation resistance.
The processed Mg-Ti-Zn alloys have substantially greater hardness than conventional commercial Mg alloys.
The initial processed alloy has improved corrosion resistance relative to conventional Mg alloys.
The proposed mechanism applies under moderate-to-high-temperature service and aqueous exposure such as 0.1 M NaCl.

contradictions.description: The initial state is defined as an already SPS-consolidated, homogeneous metastable solid solution, while the proposed decomposition and phase separation are also said to occur during SPS. The temporal point at which the homogeneous initial state exists relative to the SPS-induced transformation is therefore inconsistent or ambiguous.
